unitKey: 2Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of stateChemistry

questions.question: What is the relationship between the boiling point and condensing point of water?
options: Water boils at 100°C but condenses at 0°C.
Water condenses at 100°C and boils at 100°C.
Water boils at 100°C but condenses at room temperature (20°C).
Water condenses at 0°C and boils at 80°C.

questions.question: What is steam?
options: Liquid water droplets suspended in the air.
Water in the solid state.
Water in the gas state.
A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen gas.

questions.question: What happens to the volume of a substance when it condenses from a gas into a liquid?
options: Its volume increases.
Its volume decreases in the liquid state.
Its volume remains exactly the same.
Its volume instantly drops to zero.

questions.question: What happens to the spacing of particles when a liquid is boiled to form a gas?
options: The particles move further apart.
The particles move closer together.
The particles remain the same distance apart but grow larger.
The particles split into smaller sub-particles.

questions.question: How does the flame of a Bunsen burner change when you open the air hole?
options: It changes from a blue flame to a cooler, yellow safety flame.
It changes from an orange, sooty flame to a hotter, cleaner, blue flame.
It changes from a hot blue flame to a bright white, sparking flame.
It changes from a silent green flame to a roaring orange flame.

questions.question: What is the correct and safe way to carry a lit splint in a laboratory?
options: Pointing straight upwards to keep the flame away from your hand.
Moving as fast as possible with the flame held horizontally.
With the flame angled slightly downwards and shielded by your other hand.
Held upside down with the flame pointing directly at the floor.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the energy levels of different states of matter of the same substance?
options: Liquid states have the least energy, and solid states have the most energy.
Solid states have the least energy, and gas states have the most energy.
Gas states have the least energy, and liquid states have the most energy.
Solid, liquid, and gas states all contain the exact same amount of energy.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about evaporation?
options: A liquid can only turn into a gas when it reaches its boiling point.
Evaporation only occurs when a substance is in its solid state.
A substance in its liquid state can evaporate at temperatures below its boiling point.
Evaporation requires the temperature to be at 100°C for all liquids.

questions.question: How does temperature affect the rate at which water evaporates?
options: Water evaporates at the same rate regardless of temperature.
The colder the water, the more quickly it evaporates.
The hotter the water, the more quickly it evaporates.
Water only evaporates when it is frozen.

questions.question: A puddle of water on the ground slowly disappears on a cool autumn day at 15°C. Why does this happen?
options: Puddles can only disappear if the ground temperature reaches 100°C.
Water can evaporate at temperatures that are lower than 100°C.
The water must have sunk directly into the solid rock below.
Water only turns into vapor when it is boiling.

questions.question: How do the melting point and freezing point of a pure substance compare to each other?
options: They are the same temperature.
The melting point is always 10°C higher than the freezing point.
The freezing point is always twice as high as the melting point.
There is no relationship between the two temperatures.

questions.question: Why do solids have a fixed shape and cannot easily change their form?
options: The particles are moving very quickly in random directions.
Forces of attraction between particles hold them in fixed positions.
There are no forces of attraction holding the particles together.
The particles are extremely large and cannot move past one another.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the behavior of particles in a liquid state?
options: Particles are locked in fixed positions and can only vibrate.
Particles are held together but have enough energy to break free to move around.
Particles have completely escaped all attractive forces and fill the entire room.
Particles are stationary and do not move or vibrate at all.

questions.question: Substance A has a much higher melting point than Substance B. What does this tell us about the forces of attraction between their particles?
options: Substance A has weaker forces of attraction between its particles than Substance B.
Substance A has stronger forces of attraction between its particles than Substance B.
Both substances have no forces of attraction between their particles.
Substance B has heavier particles that prevent it from melting easily.

questions.question: Which set of temperatures is correct for water freezing, typical room temperature, and human body temperature?
options: Water freezes at 10°C, room temperature is 37°C, body temperature is 100°C.
Water freezes at 0°C, room temperature is 20°C, body temperature is 37°C.
Water freezes at -5°C, room temperature is 15°C, body temperature is 98°C.
Water freezes at 0°C, room temperature is 37°C, body temperature is 20°C.

questions.question: Which of the following properties is characteristic of a substance in its gas state?
options: It has a fixed shape, cannot flow, and cannot be compressed.
It has a fixed volume, can flow, and cannot be compressed.
It can flow, fills the whole of a container, and can be compressed.
It fills the bottom of a container, has a fixed shape, and is easily compressed.

questions.question: What exists in the spaces between the particles of a pure gas?
options: Air
Tiny particles of dust
Nothing at all
Liquid water

questions.question: What are the physical properties of a substance in its solid state?
options: It has a fixed shape, does not flow, and cannot be compressed.
It takes the shape of its container, flows easily, and can be compressed.
It has a fixed shape, can flow, and can be easily compressed.
It expands to fill any container, does not flow, and cannot be compressed.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the properties of a substance in the liquid state?
options: It has a fixed shape, does not flow, and cannot be compressed.
It can flow, fills the shape of its container, and cannot be compressed.
It can flow, fills the whole of its container, and can be compressed.
It cannot flow, takes the shape of its container, and can be compressed.

questions.question: Why can we not see the individual particles that make up a block of ice or a glass of water?
options: The particles only exist when the substance is heated into a gas.
All substances are made of particles that are too small to see.
The particles are transparent and blend in with light.
The particles only form when we look at them under a standard magnifying glass.
